parts.label: main
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests are not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement; S5 only covers binomial proportion and Normal mean tests, and S2.4 explicitly limits significance tests to those in Section 5.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly lists systematic sampling as a technique students must be familiar with.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly lists stratified sampling as a technique students must be familiar with.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S1.1 requires students to select/critique sampling techniques including comparing advantages and disadvantages.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly extends hypothesis testing language to correlation coefficients, with hypotheses on rho=0, use of critical value/p-value and calculator-computed r; use of the formula is not required but calculator use is. This matches the statement's guidance exactly, so full marks achievable in-spec.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is not named or described in any 9MA0 statement (only PMCC/product moment correlation coefficient is mentioned in S5.1).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec Spearman's rank correlation coefficient from part (b), which is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency including mean from grouped/discrete frequency data.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: The Poisson distribution is not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement (S4 only covers the discrete uniform, binomial and Normal distributions), so this part, which requires computing a Poisson probability, is out of spec even though the arithmetic itself is simple.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: Requires computing a Poisson probability and depends on the out-of-spec Poisson model; Poisson is not named in any statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for Poisson distribution
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests and the Poisson distribution are both absent from the 9MA0 statements; S2.4 restricts significance tests to those in Section 5, which does not include chi-squared or Poisson-fit tests.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Two-sample z test for difference of means
parts.reason: S5.3 only covers a hypothesis test for the mean of a single Normal distribution with known/assumed variance; a two-sample test for the difference of two means is not described by any statement.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec two-sample hypothesis test from part (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Confidence interval for a Normal mean
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements (S5.3 covers hypothesis testing for a Normal mean but not confidence interval construction).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Unbiased estimates of population mean and variance
parts.reason: Unbiased estimation (with divisor n-1) from sample sums is not described in any statement; S2.3 only covers calculating standard deviation of a data set, not unbiased population variance estimation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Standard error of combined sample mean
parts.reason: Combining samples and computing standard error of the mean is not covered by any 9MA0 statement (S5.3 explicitly excludes large-sample/CLT-type approximations and does not cover standard error calculations of this kind).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Linear combination of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: S4.2 covers the Normal distribution as a model and probability calculation but does not mention linear combinations of independent Normal variables (finding mean/variance of a combination); this is not stated anywhere in 9MA0.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Probability involving ratio/linear combination of Normal variables
parts.reason: Requires forming and using the distribution of a linear combination of Normal random variables, which is not covered by any statement (S4.2 does not mention combinations of random variables).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Distribution of sample mean / linear combination of Normal variables
parts.reason: Requires the distribution of a linear combination involving the sample mean of several Normal variables, which is not covered by any 9MA0 statement; S5.3 explicitly excludes knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or related large-sample approximations, and no statement covers combinations of Normal variables generally.
